_about: Formal definition of the record tiers (BACKLOG B12). Until now `tier` was a label with no enforced meaning: 150 records carry no tier (implying flagship) but only 41 of them have `access` and 100 have `patron`, while 410 compact records DO carry `story`. The tier said nothing about the record.
_policy: A tier is a promise about which fields are present, nothing more. It is never a quality judgement, and a record is never promoted by inventing a field (CLAUDE.md rule 2). Promotion happens when a sourced fact is added.
_enforcement: scripts/validate-data.mjs checks `tier` is one of these keys (ERROR). Per-tier field requirements are reported by scripts/report-health.mjs and become gate warnings once the backlog is cleared.

stub.label: Gazetteer stub
stub.summary: Enough to place it on the map and prove it exists.
stub.ui: Must never look broken. Show what exists plus a 'help complete this' call to action (BACKLOG B10).

compact.label: Compact record
compact.summary: The essentials: what it is, when, to whom, and why it matters.
compact.ui: Full page, no completion prompt for optional fields.

flagship.label: Flagship record
flagship.summary: A reference-grade entry: documented history AND legend AND how to get there AND who paid for it.

also_expects.non_wikipedia_source: At least one source that is not Wikipedia. 84% of the corpus is currently Wikipedia-only; a flagship record should not be.

flagship.ui: Full page with access panel, patron line, and the katha shown under its own heading, never blended with significance (CLAUDE.md rule 3).
